title: Quickstart UI mockup obfuscation and responsive crop guidelines
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define a repeatable, automated pipeline and design guidelines to produce brand-consistent quickstart screenshots and docs visuals that are privacy-safe, responsive across aspect ratios, and localization-friendly. Deliverables: crop heuristics, redaction rules, placeholder templates, color/contrast enforcement, QA checklist, and automation spec for ingestion -> transform -> export.
links: Engineering dependency for OCR redaction service: ENG-2418
comments: 2026-02-20 — Aisha Kumar: Created ticket with initial goals after design sync. Key constraints: preserve brand presence, avoid showing live customer data, support LTR/RTL localizations, and keep assets under 150KB for docs pages.

2026-02-23 — Evelyn Park: Rounded up example quickstart flows and pulled 24 sample screenshots from product staging. Noted frequent dense text regions (api keys, emails) and corner badges that need clipping preservation.

2026-02-27 — Design review: Decided on three output sizes (desktop hero 1200x560, docs inline 720x360, mobile 480x320) and two crop modes: "safe-center" and "content-aware". Trade-off: content-aware crops risk cutting small UI affordances; fallback to safe-center for critical product flows.

2026-03-02 — Engineering sync (ENG-2418): Agreed to build an OCR+masking microservice that returns redaction masks and text bounding boxes. Engineering asked for deterministic mask output (seeded) to keep snapshots stable across runs.

2026-03-04 — Accessibility pass (internal): Added contrast enforcement step — any overlay/placeholder must meet WCAG AA on contrast ratio. For low-contrast product themes, we will apply a branded translucent scrub layer to meet contrast without altering the underlying UI colors.

2026-03-06 — Localization team feedback: For RTL languages we must flip horizontal UI and re-evaluate safe-area heuristics. Also agreed to reserve a 10% vertical crop margin for locale-specific disclaimers and legal strings.

2026-03-09 — UX research: Ran quick A/B with 8 participants comparing blurred vs placeholder obfuscation. Result: participants preferred blurred overlays for context retention but flagged privacy concerns when small text remained legible. Decision: default to blurred for large regions, pattern-mask (noise tile) for short text fields and PII.

2026-03-12 — Implementation notes from Evelyn: Drafted structured export naming: quickstart/{locale}/{size}/{flow_name}/{variant}.png and metadata .json alongside each image containing crop_mode, mask_hash, generation_seed, original_screenshot_sha. Will include these in the automation manifest for reproducibility.
Open action: finalize fallback rules for content-aware crop failures and write unit tests for mask stability (ENG-2418 + DES-50123).
design_decisions: Prefer blurred region with subtle grain for large UI areas; use repeating pattern masks for PII like emails, tokens, and payment fields.
Three canonical output sizes to optimize docs and marketing reuse; derive smaller sizes from the largest using constrained downscale, not fresh crops.
Use a seeded deterministic algorithm for content-aware crops to avoid visual diffs in downstream docs pipelines.
Enforce WCAG AA for any overlay/backdrop contrasts; implement branded scrub layer for low-contrast product themes.
Locale-safe layout: always reserve top and bottom gutters (10% each) and ensure legal text boxes are injected during export rather than baked into source screenshots.
Fallback rules: if OCR confidence < 0.6 or mask coverage < 20px height for suspected PII, switch to full-region pattern-mask and mark as 'manual-review-required'.
qa_checklist: Verify masks correctly remove emails, tokens, and API keys from visual outputs (sample set of 50 staging screenshots).
Confirm cropping keeps primary CTA visible in each size variant for 95% of flows.
Run contrast analyzer on overlays and scrub layers; all outputs must pass automated WCAG AA check.
Spot-check RTL outputs to ensure horizontal flips do not break icon placement or text truncation.
Compare generated asset SHA against previous run to validate deterministic behavior when inputs and seed are unchanged.
Manual sign-off on any image marked 'manual-review-required' with reviewer name and date recorded in the manifest.
Performance: pipeline should process a single screenshot end-to-end (OCR + crop + export) in < 3s median on staging infra; if >10s mark for optimization.
File-size target: hero PNGs < 150KB, docs inline < 90KB, mobile < 60KB; compress with lossless steps and optional palette reduction for simple UIs.
automation_spec: Ingestion: poll S3 'staging/screenshots/quickstart' for new images and metadata (flow_id, locale, timestamp).
OCR & detection: call ENG-2418 OCR service to extract text boxes, PII confidence, and UI element bounding boxes.
Masking: apply deterministic mask rules (pattern for PII tokens, blur for data-dense regions).
Crop selection: run content-aware heuristic (edge-density + element-focus score) with fallback to safe-center mode.
Overlay injection: apply branded scrub/backdrop, add locale footer text if required, and enforce contrast rules.
Export: generate PNG and companion JSON manifest (crop_mode, mask_hash, seed, input_sha, size_variant, locale, review_flag).
Audit log: write entries to central assets index and emit events for Console to pick up for rollouts and docs sync.
Retry semantics: 3 attempts with exponential backoff; on repeated failure mark artifact 'failed' and create manual QA ticket.
Metric collection: pipeline latency histogram, mask-stability rate, manual-review ratio, and compress success rate.
